newsitem.title: UK: Unilever sells Nordsee fish unit to Apax.
newsitem.headline: Unilever sells Nordsee fish unit to Apax.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch consumer products giant Unilever said on Monday it sold its Nordsee fish restaurant, wholesale and retail business to Apax Partners for an undisclosed sum.
Unilever said the price for Nordsee, which had annual sales of about 390 million pounds ($636.5 million), was not material in relation to its assets.
Apax, a fund management firm, will take over Nordsee immediately and have two seats on the supervisory board, Unilever said in a statement released here.
The company said the sale was part of its plan to focus on its consumer goods businesses.

The sale will not affect the Norda-Lysell canned fish products marketed by Unilever's Union Deutsche Lebensmittelwerke, or Frozen Food International, which supplies frozen fish to associated companies in Europe.
Nordsee has 307 restaurants, with 276 in Germany and 31 in Austria.
Unilever's shares rose 22.5 pence to 16.42-1/2 stg in London by 0915 GMT.
